about.title: Carlsbad Medical Malpractice Claims
about.longDescription: Carlsbad residents rarely expect a routine appointment, outpatient procedure, or emergency visit to leave them worse off than when they arrived. When it does happen, the questions come fast. Medical malpractice in California is governed by a set of rules known as MICRA, and those rules are strict. In most cases you have one year from the date you discovered the harm, and never more than three years from the injury, to file. A 90-day notice must go to the provider before a lawsuit begins. Nearly every claim also requires a qualified medical expert to explain what a careful provider should have done differently, because a disappointing result on its own does not amount to negligence. For a community of roughly 113,000 people served by hospitals and clinics across San Diego County, that is a lot to sort through while you are still recovering. We offer a free consultation so you can ask your questions and discuss your case with an attorney who handles these claims on contingency.

items.title: MICRA's clock is short
items.desc: California generally gives you one year from discovering the harm and no more than three years from the injury itself. Getting started early leaves room for the required 90-day pre-suit notice.

items.title: Expert testimony is nearly always required
items.desc: A qualified medical expert must usually confirm that the care fell below the accepted standard. We know how to evaluate whether that opinion is realistic before you invest time in a claim.

items.title: Free consultation, contingency-based representation
items.desc: We offer a free case review and handle malpractice cases on contingency, meaning no fee unless there is a recovery.

items.question: I was treated in a Carlsbad emergency room after a crash on I-5 and a fracture was missed. Is that malpractice?
items.answer: It might be, but a missed finding is not automatically negligence. The question is whether a reasonably careful emergency physician, given the same symptoms and imaging, would have caught it. With hundreds of injury collisions reported in Carlsbad each year, ER visits after crashes on I-5, Palomar Airport Road, or El Camino Real are common, and a qualified medical expert would need to review your records to say whether the standard of care was met.

items.question: Is there a limit on what I can recover in a California medical malpractice case?
items.answer: California caps non-economic damages such as pain and suffering in malpractice cases, and that cap rises each year under MICRA. Economic losses like medical bills and lost income are treated separately. We can explain how the current figures apply to your specific situation.

items.question: How long do I have to act if the mistake happened in Carlsbad?
items.answer: The general rule is one year from the date you discovered, or reasonably should have discovered, the injury, and no later than three years from the date the injury occurred. Before filing suit, a 90-day notice must be sent to the provider. Because those windows can overlap in confusing ways, it is worth speaking with an attorney sooner rather than later.
